summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and severe sclerodermatous graft-versus-host disease was admitted for shortness of breath and a low-grade fever. Evaluation revealed no evidence of active infection, with negative respiratory viral testing and blood cultures. Chest imaging showed improvement from prior studies with no new infiltrates. His dyspnea resolved during the hospital stay and was attributed to underlying restrictive lung disease from GVHD. Liver enzymes were elevated but stable and asymptomatic, likely due to medication effects. Chronic lower extremity wounds showed bacterial colonization without signs of active infection. All home medications, including immunosuppressants, antibiotics, and pain management, were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up on liver function and continue specialty care.
